## Report

# CBT formats for depressed teenagers

A network meta-analysis of 62 randomised trials with 6435 participants found that most CBT formats, except remote CBT, did better than no intervention after treatment \[1\].

The same review found that guided self-help was clearly better than every other format, with a SUCRA of 83% \[1\].

A university news release said that technology-assisted CBT for children and young people is just as effective as face-to-face CBT in 7 trials \[2\].

Across psychotherapy trials, about 39% of young people responded to therapy, against 24% in control conditions.

## Sources

1. [A comparison of the effectiveness of cognitive behavioural interventions](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10771715/)
